description.zh-CN: 在 3D 空间中搭建场景并进行多视角截图。
description.en-US: Build scenes in 3D space and capture multi-angle screenshots.

details.zh-CN: 在用户选择导演台或正在编辑其场景时，摆放三维角色和道具、调整姿态、设置机位与运镜，输出分镜预演参考。支持标准男女与儿童素体、自定义 GLB/GLTF 模型。仅提到分镜、三维或动画不代表选择本插件；已有 Blender、Photoshop 或 After Effects 制作不切换到导演台。不用于平面分镜生图、最终高精度渲染或完整成片。
details.en-US: When the user selects Director Stage or edits its scene, stage 3D characters and props, pose them, and rehearse cameras and movement for previz references. Supports male, female and child mannequins and custom GLB/GLTF models. Storyboard, 3D or animation words alone do not select this plugin. Keep existing Blender, Photoshop or After Effects work in its chosen application. Not for flat storyboard generation, final-quality rendering or finished films.

methods.name: scene.get
methods.description:
Read the authoritative structured scene. args: {}. Returns revision, summary and codeModels/characters/props/models/cameras/camPaths/timeline/customMotions/groups/environment/selectedIds.

Transforms include unrounded position/rotation/scale/uniformScale values; character color/pose/bodyType and object visibility/locks are included. camPaths include up to the first 64 control points, `pointsCount`, `pointsTruncated`, look target/point, duration/easing/loop/FOV and dsl flag; use campath.read for complete editable DSL source when available. Timeline clips include id/ref/start/duration/enabled. Environment includes writable background, panorama, sky, ground and scene transform fields. Positions are meters, rotations degrees, timeline values milliseconds.

Use it before edits when <editor_state> is stale/truncated, and after editing to verify exact state. It is structural data, not visual evidence; use scene.snapshot and inspect the JPEG for framing, occlusion and appearance.

methods.name: model.generate
model.capture
methods.description:
Render a code model offscreen from canonical views for visual review. args: { id?, views?, size?, layout? }.
- id: code-model id (prefix ok); omitted = first code model.
- views: subset of ["front","back","left","right","top","three_quarter","three_quarter_back"]; default ["front","three_quarter","left","top"]. Renders use a neutral light-grey studio (no grid/gizmos/other scene objects); hidden parts stay hidden.
- size: square pixels per view 256–1280 (default 768).
- layout: "grid" (default) | "separate". Grid composes ALL requested views into ONE row-major contact-sheet JPEG, each cell labeled with its view name, and returns { ok, id, path, width, height, grid: [{ view, row, col }], referencePath }. Separate returns one clean unlabeled JPEG per view as { ok, id, captures: [{ view, path }], referencePath } — it exists ONLY for feeding model.compare (grid labels/neighboring cells corrupt its pixel metrics) and allows at most 2 views per call; all multi-view visual review goes through the grid sheet.
Each path is a workspace-relative JPEG in the staging area (.hilo/.tmp/uploads/) — read it with your media analysis tool and compare against the reference image view-by-view. Every view has an expected silhouette (a bike: front = narrow/wheels edge-on, left = two full circles, top = a thin strip — round wheel discs seen from above mean wheels lying flat or mounted sideways); ALL views (all grid cells) must be self-consistent with the intended layout — one plausible angle is not evidence, and a layout that only works from one view is wrong (a sideways wheel looks like a perfect circle exactly when viewed along its normal). Captures are temporary evidence files, not canvas assets. This is the ONLY way you can see the model; never claim visual fidelity without capturing and looking first.

methods.name: model.compare
methods.description:
Deterministic 2D comparison gate between a capture and the reference image (runs the plugin's bundled Python; first call may take ~1 min to build the venv). args: { renderPath, referencePath } — both workspace-relative (renderPath from model.capture with layout:"separate" — never a grid contact sheet, whose labels and neighboring cells corrupt the metrics; referencePath from the generate request).
Returns { ok, silhouette_iou, aspect_ratio { render, reference, delta_ratio }, color_similarity, grid_diff_4x4_row_major[], worst_cell { row, col, diff }, composite_score, verdict }.
- silhouette_iou: foreground-silhouette overlap after bbox-crop normalization (composition-independent shape match). grid_diff locates WHERE the silhouette deviates (row 0 = top).
- Use as advisory evidence between iterations: silhouette_iou < ~0.6 or aspect delta_ratio > ~0.15 usually means wrong proportions. Compare only a capture whose view matches the reference's viewpoint (a left-view reference against the left capture); comparing mismatched views produces meaningless scores — judge the other captures by self-consistency instead. Metrics are blind to materials, lighting and 3D form — a passing score is NOT acceptance; visual inspection of captures remains the authority. Best on single-object references with clean backgrounds; on cluttered scenes trust your eyes instead.

methods.name: scene.edit
methods.description:
Atomically validate or apply an ordered scene batch as ONE undo step.

args: { description: string, operations: object[1..50], validateOnly?: boolean }.
Returns { ok, validateOnly, applied, failed, rolledBack:false, results:[{index,type,ok,code?,detail?,id?,warnings?,candidates?}], affectedIds[], summary, revision, note? }.

All operations execute against a pure draft. Any failure means ZERO scene writes; fix the reported operation and resend the whole batch. validateOnly:true runs the same draft validation and applies nothing. A later operation can reference an object created by operations[N] as "$N" (0-based); referencing a future or non-creating operation returns INVALID_REFERENCE. Exact ids win; a prefix must match exactly one object or returns AMBIGUOUS_ID with candidates.

Operations:
- add_character {position, bodyType?, pose?, rotationY?, label?, color?, uniformScale?}. bodyType: mannequin|female|child. poses: stand,tpose,walk,run,jump,sit,squat,kneel,lie,drive,wave,hands_up,bow,akimbo,think,fight,aim,sword,spell. Ground poses keep position.y=0; sit/drive plant the hips exactly at position.y — set y to the seat-top height (bench ≈0.48, chair/stool ≈0.45, sofa ≈0.40, × the seat prop's uniformScale — e.g. bench at uniformScale 1.2 → y=0.576), otherwise the character sits on the ground. A seated character must also face the seat's outward direction: set rotationY equal to the seat prop's rotationY (catalog seats face +Z before rotation) or the character sits sideways across the bench. Driving the catalog car: the car is a CLOSED low-poly body — its cabin renders as opaque dark glass, so a driver seated inside is INVISIBLE from outside. Character scale is STATIC for the whole timeline (paths drive position/rotation only), so choose by the beat that matters most: (a) driver never leaves the car → hips y≈0.8, uniformScale≈0.5, |x offset| ≤ 0.35, z within ±0.7 of the cabin (× car uniformScale), fully hidden with no limbs clipping the walls; (b) driver must later stand/walk beside props at natural size → keep uniformScale 1, seat hips at y≈0.8 and let the head stand proud of the roofline (reads as a convertible in wide shots) — NEVER shrink a character who appears on foot in a later beat, and never promise a visible driver through the closed glass; to show the driver, stop the car and stage a step-out beat (short move path to beside the door + stand/walk anims, static pose stand at the final mark).
- add_prop {assetId,position,rotationY?,scale?,uniformScale?,label?}. Props render in fixed materials — geo meshes are all light-blue primitive and CANNOT be recolored, so never use them for color-critical elements (fire, blood, foliage); build those from colored catalog props (lamps for glow, rocks/plants for organics) or a code model (full color control). Catalog ids:
  geo mesh_cube,mesh_sphere,mesh_cylinder,mesh_torus,mesh_cone,mesh_pyramid,mesh_rectangle,mesh_disc,mesh_capsule,mesh_arc,mesh_half_cylinder;
  furniture chair,stool,armchair,sofa,square_table,desk,round_table,bed,bookshelf,cabinet,wardrobe,tv,wall_tv,floor_lamp,table_lamp,rug;
  building wall,column,staircase,ramp,platform,arch,door,fence,ladder,statue;
  nature tree_small,tree_large,rock,bush,potted_plant,stump,flower_bed;
  street car,truck,bicycle,streetlamp,bench,trash_bin,traffic_cone,road_barrier,sign,fire_hydrant,barrel,crate.
  A prop must semantically match what it plays; a recognizable object missing from this catalog (a campfire, a guitar…) is model.generate territory — not a repurposed prop or a multi-prop stand-in.
- set_pose {id,pose}. Switching to/from sit or drive: also set_transform the character's position.y to the seat top (or back to 0).
- add_campath {preset?,center?,radius?,height?,startDeg?,points?,targetId?,lookAt?,duration?,easing?,clipStart?,label?}. preset: orbit|arc|dolly_in|dolly_out|dolly_zoom|crane_up|crane_down|truck|spiral. Otherwise points is >=2 waypoints. easing: linear|easeIn|easeOut|easeInOut|smoothstep. Creates path + camera-track clip.
- set_campath {dsl,id?,clipStart?,label?}. Omit id to create path+clip; pass id to replace path geometry/source in place. Existing timeline clips keep their layout; clipStart is ignored with a warning on update. Use campath.read before revising.
- add_move_path {targetId,points,duration?,orient?,clipStart?,label?}. target character/prop; orient follow|keep. Creates path + object track. With follow, the LAST segment's heading is the character's final facing (held after the clip ends, used at timeline end) — aim the final segment at the scene partner/goal so arrival lands facing them; approaches to a person stop 1.2–1.6m short, walking the last step toward them.
- set_motion {dsl,id?,label?}. Omit id to create; id updates custom motion. Built-ins are read-only. Use motion.read as a template.
- add_anim_clip {targetId,animId,start?,duration?}. Built-ins: idle,walk,run,jump,talk,sit_talk,wave,bow,cheer,dance,punch,death; custom motion ids and "$N" work. Never stack duplicate/overlapping clips for one beat on one track (only the later-starting clip evaluates; extras are defects — remove them). To end the timeline holding a mid-action phase (e.g. a bow still held down), trim the clip's duration so the timeline ends inside that phase, before the animation recovers.
- set_environment {skyColor?,backgroundMode?,showGround?,groundOpacity?,groundHeight?}. backgroundMode flat|panorama.
- set_camera {id?,position?,lookAt?,fov?}. Omit id for first camera; fov 10..120.
- set_transform {id,position?,rotationY?|rotation?,scale?,uniformScale?}. Character, prop, uploaded model, or code model.
- set_part {id,part,visible?,position?,rotation?,scale?,reset?}. Code-model named part only.
- rename {id,label}. Character, prop, code model, or camera path.
- remove {id}. Removes the entity and its direct path/motion timeline references. When a correction loop rebuilds a path or motion, remove the superseded one in the same batch — orphan paths no timeline clip references pollute the scene (diagnostics reports UNREFERENCED_PATH).

Stable operation-result codes include INVALID_PARAMS, UNKNOWN_OPERATION, INVALID_REFERENCE, OBJECT_NOT_FOUND, AMBIGUOUS_ID, DSL_INVALID, and ACTION_FAILED. A concurrent write/capture rejects the method with case-sensitive host error code `busy`. results[].warnings are advisory clamping/ignored-field notices; inspect them before reporting completion.

Creative blocking and camera language live in the market skill director-stage. DSL syntax lives in the plugin runtime reference; this method document is the exact operation catalog.

methods.name: scene.history
methods.description:
Step the current editor-session history. args: { action: "undo"|"redo", steps?: number } where steps defaults to 1 and is clamped to 1..20.

Returns { ok, action, stepsTaken, canUndo, canRedo, undoDepth, redoDepth, summary, revision }. stepsTaken can be smaller than requested at the stack boundary. One successful scene.edit batch is one history level. History is session-local and is not persisted when the editor is closed.

methods.name: scene.snapshot
methods.description:
Capture the real browser-rendered full scene as clean JPEG staging file(s). args: { cameraId?: string, aspect?: "auto"|"16:9"|"4:3"|"1:1"|number, atTimes?: number[], layout?: "sheet"|"separate" }.

Without cameraId, captures the current viewport. With a unique camera id/prefix, temporarily renders from that scene camera and then restores the user's exact viewport in finally. Helpers, gizmos and camera models are hidden. Returns { ok, path, width, height, view:"current"|"camera", cameraId, revision, hint }. Width/height are the actual capture dimensions; output follows the mounted viewport/DPR and aspect crop.

atTimes (1..8 timeline milliseconds) captures one frame per entry with the composed timeline fully evaluated at that instant — camera clips, character/prop move paths and animation clips all applied, exactly like scrubbing the playhead. Use it to review motion beats after timeline edits: sample each clip's start/middle/end and the frames just before/after a camera cut. Requires a timeline with clips; values clamp to [0, duration]. Without cameraId each frame uses the timeline's composed camera (viewport view where no camera clip covers that time); with cameraId all frames are shot from that fixed camera while characters still move. Afterwards driven objects reset to their static transforms and the user's viewport is restored. Rejected with `busy` while timeline preview or the virtual camera is driving the viewport.

By default (layout "sheet") the frames are composed into labeled contact sheet(s): at most 4 cells per sheet in time order (8 frames → two sheets), each cell downscaled to ≤960px wide and tagged `t=…ms` in its top-left corner. Returns { ok, sheets:[{path,width,height,cells:[{tMs,row,col}]}], frameCount, durationMs, view:"timeline"|"camera", cameraId, revision, hint }. One sheet puts adjacent beats in the same image, which is the only way a vision tool can directly compare frames for continuity (sliding, teleports, pose pops between samples) — per-file analysis cannot cross-reference. Review every sheet, then zoom in where needed.

layout:"separate" uploads each frame as its own full-resolution JPEG and allows at most 3 atTimes per call. Returns { ok, frames:[{tMs,path,width,height}], durationMs, view, cameraId, revision, hint }. Use it as the second tier of the review funnel: after a sheet survey flags a suspicious beat (or when a judgement hinges on fine detail the downscaled cell cannot settle — small contacts, thin props, distant characters), re-capture just that tMs at full resolution. layout without atTimes is rejected: a plain snapshot is already one full-resolution frame.

`ENGINE_NOT_READY` means the editor viewport is not mounted or required scene resources are not ready. `busy` means a scene write/capture is active. `CAPTURE_FAILED` means no valid frame was produced or readiness timed out. `UPLOAD_FAILED` means staging is unavailable. Codes are case-sensitive.

The returned path(s) are evidence, not a verdict: open each with a host media/vision tool and inspect it. Never claim it was visually checked merely because this call succeeded. Diagnostics and model.compare cannot replace this scene-level visual review.

methods.name: scene.diagnostics
methods.description:
Run read-only mechanical checks over the current Composition. args: {}. Returns { ok, clean, issues:[{code,severity,detail,ids?}], summary }.

Checks duplicate ids, dangling group members, invalid track targets/types, missing path/motion clip references, non-finite or invalid transforms/scales/timing, path point count/underground points, same-track clip overlaps, duplicated same-source clip stacking (CLIP_DUPLICATE, error — remove the extra clip), and paths no timeline clip references (UNREFERENCED_PATH, warning — usually correction-loop leftovers to remove). clean means no error-severity issue; warnings require judgement.

Diagnostics do NOT render the scene and cannot approve composition, pose, occlusion, lighting or camera framing. Fix errors (or explicitly explain intentional cases), then use scene.snapshot and inspect its image for visual verification.

methods.name: motion.read
methods.description:
Read the semantic-joint DSL source of any character motion — built-in preset or scene custom motion. args: { id } (built-in id like "walk", or a custom motion id / 8-char prefix from scene.get). Returns { id, builtin, label, loop, cycleMs, defaultMs, source, warnings }.

Motions are plain text (source is the single source of truth). Typical loop: motion.read a close built-in → copy & edit its DSL → scene.edit set_motion (omit id → new custom motion) → add_anim_clip with the returned id. Use this instead of guessing DSL from scratch: built-ins are curated worked examples (e.g. read "run" for asymmetric gait cycles with explicit closing step + sink, "bow" for pelvis hinge, "death" for lying on the ground).

methods.name: campath.read
methods.description:
Read a camera path from the scene. args: { id } (a camPath id from scene.get camPaths[], 8-char prefix ok). Returns { id, label, durationMs, easing, loopMode, lookAtTarget, lookAt, points, source, waypoints?, hint }.

- source non-null → the path was authored as campath DSL (scene.edit set_campath): the text IS the truth. Typical edit loop: campath.read → tweak the DSL (retime a beat, extend an orbit, change the look target) → set_campath with the SAME id to update the geometry in place (its timeline clips keep their own start/duration).
- source null → hand-drawn / preset / phone-vcam path. waypoints[] lists its control-point positions so you can study the framing; to revise it, author a DSL replacement with set_campath passing this id (swaps geometry in place) — or leave it alone and add a new path.

Manual edits in the editor invalidate stale DSL (the host clears source when the user drags points), so a null source on a formerly DSL path means the user reshaped it by hand.

agent.instructions:
You are editing a 3D DIRECTOR STAGE scene. It contains built-in posable characters, catalog props, uploaded/code models, cameras, camera paths, a millisecond timeline, custom motion DSL, and environment settings.

CORE RULES:
- Read before changing: use the compact <editor_state> for simple known edits; call scene.get when exact transforms, ids, paths, or timeline layout matter. 8-char prefixes work only when unique; never invent ids.
- Asset routing: people use scene.edit add_character. A catalog prop is used only when it semantically IS the requested object (a crate for a crate, a tree for a tree). Any recognizable object the catalog lacks (a campfire, a guitar, a piano…) is built with model.generate — never REPURPOSE a semantically different prop (a table_lamp as a campfire) and never ASSEMBLE one named object from several props/mesh_* primitives (a sphere + a rectangle as a guitar): both read wrong in any close or medium shot and cannot be selected, transformed, or edited as one object. Bare mesh_* geometry is only for abstract filler, risers, and distant background masses that no shot resolves. Scene-dressing code props (supporting objects judged within the whole shot) are ONE model.generate call producing a rough primitive-based shape — correct proportions, silhouette, ground contact; resolve the returned warnings, then judge it in the normal scene.snapshot pass with no dedicated capture/refine loop. Only hero objects (close-up subjects, a provided reference image, or an explicit fidelity request) follow the staged build protocol in the model.generate doc (layout spec → blockout → verify → refine in place); never one-shot a multi-part hero object.
- Put all changes for one user request in ONE scene.edit call with a short user-facing description. It is an atomic transaction and one undo step. For large/risky builds, call validateOnly:true first, then resend the same corrected batch to apply.
- Batch failure changes nothing. Read the failed result's index/code/detail/candidates, fix it, and resend the whole batch. BUSY means retry after the active write settles.
- Verify structure after edits with scene.get and scene.diagnostics. Diagnostics are mechanical only; they cannot approve composition, visibility, pose quality, or camera framing. Never cite passing diagnostics (or any deterministic metric) as evidence of visual fidelity.
- For any visual scene claim, call scene.snapshot at the affected current view or camera, then actually open and inspect the returned JPEG with a host media/vision tool. A returned path alone is not visual inspection.
- Fail closed on quality: while an identity-defining feature is visibly wrong (wheel orientation, part contact, silhouette, pose ground contact, interaction facing), you may not declare the work complete. When the correction budget runs out, deliver with an explicit list of remaining mismatches instead of a success claim.
- Only touch what the user requested. Report in the user's language and never paste raw method JSON.

Times in scene methods are MILLISECONDS. Positions are meters. rotationY is degrees: 0 faces +Z, 90 faces +X, 180 faces -Z. Ground is y=0; standing/walking characters normally stay there. Seat-contact poses (sit, drive) plant the hips exactly at position.y: set y to the seat-top height (bench ≈0.48, chair/stool ≈0.45, sofa ≈0.40, × the seat's uniformScale). Leaving y=0 visibly sits the character on the ground — a classic mistake. squat/kneel/lie auto-drop to touch the ground and keep y=0. Facing matters as much as position: rotationY = atan2(dx, dz) in degrees aims self at a target (dx/dz = target minus self); seated characters face the seat's own rotationY. Interaction beats (bow, talk, hand-off) must land face-to-face — delivered to a partner's back or side they fail the beat, and with move-path orient follow the final facing comes from the path's last segment, not the static rotationY.

Creative workflow is distributed separately as the market skill `director-stage`. For creative staging, camera design, custom objects or visual review in THIS editor, load `director-stage` with the native skill tool only when that exact name is available in the current runtime catalog. If it is missing or disabled, explain that the Director Stage skill needs to be installed or enabled; never claim it was loaded. Already-authorized direct edits can still use this plugin contract. This instruction does not select Director Stage for unrelated tasks or override a user-selected application. Method docs and the runtime reference remain the authority for exact operations and fields.

Typical workflow: scene.get → optional scene.edit validateOnly → scene.edit apply → scene.diagnostics → scene.snapshot + inspect (after timeline changes, sample motion beats with atTimes, inspect every returned contact sheet cell in time order, and re-capture suspicious beats with layout:'separate' for full-resolution frames) → make one focused correction batch if needed → leave the user on a clear explanation of the scene and how to preview the timeline.
